Looking at this problem, I need to find the maximum number of students where each student solves one of 20 math problems and one of 11 physics problems, all pairs are distinct, and for each student, at least one of their two problems was solved by at most one other student (i.e., that problem has degree ≤ 2 in the bipartite graph).

**Model.** Form a bipartite graph $G$ with math problems $M$ ($|M|=20$) on one side and physics problems $P$ ($|P|=11$) on the other. Each student is an edge. The condition states: for every edge $(m,p)$, $\deg(m)\le 2$ or $\deg(p)\le 2$.

**Upper bound.**

Let $M'=\{m\in M:\deg(m)\le 2\}$, $P'=\{p\in P:\deg(p)\le 2\}$, with $a=|M'|$, $b=|P'|$. Every edge has at least one endpoint in $M'\cup P'$, so no edge connects $M\setminus M'$ to $P\setminus P'$.

Partition edges into: $E_{LL}$ (between $M'$ and $P'$), $E_{LH}$ (between $M'$ and $P\setminus P'$), $E_{HL}$ (between $M\setminus M'$ and $P'$). Then $E_{HH}=\emptyset$ and $|E|=|E_{LL}|+|E_{LH}|+|E_{HL}|$.

Degree constraints give:
$$|E_{LL}|+|E_{LH}|\le 2a,\qquad |E_{LL}|+|E_{HL}|\le 2b.$$

Adding: $2|E_{LL}|+|E_{LH}|+|E_{HL}|\le 2a+2b$, so $|E|\le 2a+2b-|E_{LL}|\le 2a+2b$.

**Case 1: $M\setminus M'\ne\emptyset$ and $P\setminus P'\ne\emptyset$.** Each vertex in $M\setminus M'$ has degree $\ge 3$, all going to $P'$, so $|E_{HL}|\ge 3(20-a)$. Similarly $|E_{LH}|\ge 3(11-b)$. The bipartite capacity gives $|E_{HL}|\le (20-a)b$ and $|E_{LH}|\le a(11-b)$.

Setting $|E_{LL}|=0$ for maximum: $|E|=|E_{LH}|+|E_{HL}|\le \min(2a,\,a(11-b))+\min(2b,\,(20-a)b)$.

- For $|E_{LH}|=2a$: need $11-b\ge 2$, i.e., $b\le 9$.
- For $|E_{HL}|=2b$: need $20-a\ge 2$, i.e., $a\le 18$.

When $b\le 9$ and $a\le 18$: $|E|\le 2a+2b\le 2(18)+2(9)=54$.

When $b\ge 10$: $|E_{LH}|\le a(11-b)\le a$, and $|E_{HL}|\le 2b$, so $|E|\le a+2b$. With $a\le 18$: $|E|\le 18+20=38<54$ (and checking $a=19$ gives even less due to capacity).

When $a\ge 19$: $|E_{HL}|\le (20-a)b\le b$, so $|E|\le 2a+b\le 38+9=47<54$.

**Case 2: $M\setminus M'=\emptyset$ ($a=20$).** All edges incident to $M'$, so $|E|\le 2(20)=40<54$.

**Case 3: $P\setminus P'=\emptyset$ ($b=11$).** All edges incident to $P'$, so $|E|\le 2(11)=22<54$.

In all cases, $|E|\le 54$.

**Construction achieving 54.** Set $a=18$, $b=9$: choose 18 math problems as $M'$ (degree 2 each) and 2 as $M\setminus M'$ (degree 9 each); choose 9 physics problems as $P'$ (degree 2 each) and 2 as $P\setminus P'$ (degree 18 each).

- $E_{LH}$: Each of the 18 $M'$-vertices connects to both 2 $P\setminus P'$-vertices: $18\times 2=36$ edges. Each $P\setminus P'$-vertex has degree 18.
- $E_{HL}$: Each of the 9 $P'$-vertices connects to both 2 $M\setminus M'$-vertices: $9\times 2=18$ edges. Each $M\setminus M'$-vertex has degree 9.
- $E_{LL}=0$.

Total: $36+18=54$ edges, all distinct. Every edge has an endpoint of degree 2 (the $M'$ or $P'$ vertex). ✓

**The maximum possible number of students is $\boxed{54}$.**
